style_1_icd10.name: Interstitial cystitis (chronic) without hematuria
style_1_icd10.chapter: XIV. Diseases of the genitourinary system / Nephrology & Urology (N00-N99)

style_2_guidelines.guideline_authority: GOLD 2024 Global Strategy for the Diagnosis, Management, and Prevention of COPD

clinical_targets.goal: mMRC dyspnea scale < 2, COPD Assessment Test (CAT) score < 10
Zero moderate-to-severe exacerbations requiring oral steroids or hospitalization
Post-bronchodilator FEV1 stabilization and hyperinflation reduction

steps_summary: Step 1: Group A: Low Symptoms & Low Exacerbation Risk
Step 2: Group B: High Symptoms & Low Exacerbation Risk
Step 3: Group E: High Exacerbation Risk (≥ 2 moderate or ≥ 1 hospitalization)

steps.title: Group A: Low Symptoms & Low Exacerbation Risk
steps.rationale: Initial therapy is a single long-acting bronchodilator (LAMA or LABA) to improve airflow and reduce dyspnea.

drug_classes.role: Preferred initial bronchodilator; greater reduction in exacerbation rate compared to LABA monotherapy.
drug_classes.dosing: Tiotropium 18 mcg dry powder inhaler (DPI) once daily or Respimat 5 mcg (2 puffs) once daily.
drug_classes.pearls: Dry mouth is the most common side effect. Use caution in patients with severe urinary retention or narrow-angle glaucoma.

steps.title: Group B: High Symptoms & Low Exacerbation Risk
steps.rationale: Dual bronchodilation (LABA + LAMA) is superior to monotherapy for symptom relief, exercise tolerance, and quality of life.

drug_classes.role: Standard of care for symptomatic COPD patients without frequent exacerbations.
drug_classes.dosing: Available in Egyptian market as single-inhaler or complementary device dual therapy.
drug_classes.pearls: Synergistic bronchodilation through complementary adrenergic and anticholinergic pathways.

steps.title: Group E: High Exacerbation Risk (≥ 2 moderate or ≥ 1 hospitalization)
steps.rationale: Dual LABA+LAMA is initial preferred therapy. Escalate to Triple Therapy (LABA+LAMA+ICS) if blood eosinophils ≥ 300 cells/µL.

drug_classes.role: Decreases exacerbations and all-cause mortality in frequent exacerbators with eosinophilic inflammation (IMPACT & ETHOS trials).
drug_classes.dosing: Single-inhaler or dual-device triple therapy taken daily.
drug_classes.pearls: ICS monotherapy is strictly CONTRAINDICATED in COPD due to increased risk of bacterial pneumonia without bronchodilator benefit.

pearls: Dry mouth is the most common side effect. Use caution in patients with severe urinary retention or narrow-angle glaucoma.
Synergistic bronchodilation through complementary adrenergic and anticholinergic pathways.
ICS monotherapy is strictly CONTRAINDICATED in COPD due to increased risk of bacterial pneumonia without bronchodilator benefit.

special_populations.cardiovascular_disease: COPD patients frequently have comorbid CAD or heart failure. Cardioselective beta-1 blockers (Bisoprolol) are SAFE and beneficial in COPD when indicated.
special_populations.chronic_hypoxemia: Long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT) indicated if resting PaO2 ≤ 55 mmHg or SaO2 ≤ 88% to improve survival.

style_3_monograph.summary: Interstitial cystitis (IC) is a condition that causes discomfort or pain in the bladder and a need to urinate frequently and urgently. It is far more common in women than in men. The symptoms vary from person to person. Some people may have pain without urgency or frequency. Others have urgency and frequency without pain. Women's symptoms often get worse during their periods. They may also have pain with sexual intercourse. The cause of IC isn't known. There is no one test to tell if you have it. Doctors often run tests to rule out other possible causes of symptoms. There is no cure for IC, but treatments can help most people feel better. They include: Distending, or inflating, the bladder Bathing the inside of the bladder with a drug solution Oral medicines Electrical nerve stimulation Physical therapy Lifestyle changes Bladder training In rare cases, surgery NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
style_3_monograph.treatment: Consult healthcare provider for individualized management.
